For degree d>=3, this requires at least 1+d+d(d-1)+d(d-1)^2 vertices (22 for d=3). Thus on 14 vertices, max degree <=2, so the graph is disjoint paths/cycles (>=8). Max edges is 14 (from C_14), but 29>14, hence impossible.

results.reasoning: Graphs on 15 vertices with girth >=8 have maximum degree mostly <=2 (trees or unicyclic with cycles >=8), yielding at most 15 edges. Higher degrees require branching vertices separated by distance ~4 with paths ensuring all cycles >=8. Constructions (e.g., multiple paths between 2-3 high-degree vertices) achieve at most ~17-18 edges before short cycles (C3-C7) appear due to pigeonhole on path lengths/multiplicities or insufficient vertices (Moore-like: deg>=3 vertex with branching needs ~10-22 exclusive verts). For 24 edges, sum(deg-2)=18 implies ~9+ high-degree vertices or high multiplicities, forcing support graph on them to have 18+ edges, which (even if triangle-free) creates weighted cycles summing to <8. Bipartite case limits to <=22 edges even without C4 alone (sum binom(d_y,2) <= binom(7,2)=21). Thus, impossible to reach 24 edges.

results.reasoning: A graph with 18 vertices and at least 27 edges has average degree exactly 3 (for 27 edges). This requires the degree sequence to balance around 3 (e.g., four degree-4 vertices and four degree-2 vertices with the rest degree-3, or similar variations). For girth >=7, the ball of radius 3 around any degree-4 vertex must form a tree. Unfolding this tree with the available low-degree vertices to minimize its size yields a minimum |B(v,3)| of 17 only in the marginal case where all four degree-2 vertices are direct neighbors of one degree-4 vertex. The remaining structure requires at least 11 additional edges among the 9 peripheral vertices to reach 27 total edges. However, these peripheral edges must create cycles of length >=7 without forming C3-C6 when combined with tree paths. The 4 pairs of 'sibling' leaves (children of the same level-2 vertex) must maintain distance >=5 in the peripheral graph to avoid C<=6. With 11 edges on 9 vertices (exceeding the tree maximum of 8), a cycle in the peripheral graph is required, needing a component of size >=7. Yet, separating all sibling pairs limits any component to size <=5, preventing long cycles. Adding edges while maintaining distances >=5 for siblings also fails, as any chord shortens at least one critical distance, creating forbidden cycles <=6. Lower variations in degrees yield |B(v,3)| >18, which is impossible. Thus, no such graph exists.
